newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 30.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 30.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

NEW YORK - Ad agency Bozell, Jacobs Kenyon & Eckhardt is being courted by Omnicom Group Inc and True North Communications, which are both seeking to buy the firm in a deal worth about $400 million, according to newspaper reports.
WASHINGTON - Diet products company Jenny Craig must warn consumers in its advertising that its weight loss methods are usually only temporary, the federal government says.

BETHEL, Connecticut - Duracell North Atlantic Group says it will air new TV spots in an advertising campaign to meet Energizer head-on in the battle for battery superiority. The new ads were created by Ogilvy & Mather Advertising.

LONDON - Britain's top financial regulator, the Securities and Investments Board, launches a 400,000 pound ($654,000) advertising campaign designed to heighten the public's awareness of a review into pensions misselling. Under the banner, "Have You Lost Out On Your Pension?", the campaign seeks to underline the importance of the public playing its part in the review.

COPENHAGEN - France Telecom's Danish unit, Mobilix, has budgeted 50 million crowns ($7.7 million) for advertising to launch its Danish mobile telephone service, advertising business journal Markedsfoering says.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - AOL, the online information joint venture of America Online and Germany's Bertelsmann, says it is starting online advertising in France. Companies like IBM, Microsoft, Canon, and Perrier are already planning to advertise on AOL France.

LUXEMBOURG - European Union countries may not block television broadcasts transmitted from other member states, even if they do not meet European-based programming rules, the European Court of Justice rules. Under the EU's "television without frontiers" law, EU television channels are required to devote over half their screen time to European programmes "where practicable".

VIENNA, Virginia - Advertising revenue for the first quarter of 1997 injected $8.9 billion into the newspaper industry, an increase of nearly nine percent over the same period last year, the Newspaper Association of America says.

HAMBURG - Pay-TV station Premiere says it continued its growth trend in May. With over 30,000 new subscriptions, the stations says it surpassed last years's record expansion of 26,000. Premiere says its expects to set further growth records in June with the broadcast of popular films and sports events.

MEXICO CITY - Mexican media group Televisa says it has agreed a resource-sharing accord with U.S. broadcaster NBC, a unit of General Electric. Under the agreement its 24-hour financial news channel "Conexin Financiera" will begin transmitting programming from NBC affiliate CNBC.

BEIJING - China's propaganda tsars will axe 300 newspapers in one year as part of a shake-up of an industry seen as tainted by corruption and ideas out of line with Communist Party ideology, the official Ningxia Daily says.

CHICAGO - The Chicago Sun-Times says it plans to build a $100 million printing plant and will buy six web offset presses from Goss Graphic Systems Inc for the facility, which is expected to be operating by the end of 1999.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
NEW YORK - McDonald's Corp has decided not to guarantee to customers in the U.S. that it can deliver their orders within 55 seconds of having paid for them, the Wall Street Journal says.
LONDON - Spirits packaged in plastic sachets under the brand name Totpak violate British marketing guidelines by appealing to underage drinkers, industry watchdog the Portman Group says.

MILAN - Over half of computer software applications used in Italy last year were pirated, resulting in a total loss of revenue of some 580 billion lire ($343.7 million), a study from the Business Software Alliance says.

JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma, spurred by the country's high alcohol consumption, is considering measures to package alcoholic drinks with health warnings, a government spokesman says.

LONDON - Sir Rocco Forte, who lost control of his Forte hotel empire last year to Granada Group Plc, signs contracts to commence work on the first of a new chain of hotels to be set up throughout Russia.
LONDON - The European paging market is poised to shake off its lethargy and triple to over 18 million subscribers by the year 2001, industry experts say.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

FUSCHL, Austria - Europe's clubbers are using Austria's Red Bull energy drink mixed with vodka to give them pep on the dance floor. The product takes 90 percent of the domestic energy drink market and a 30 percent share in Europe, and its success shows no signs of fizzling out.
SINGAPORE - It took the U.S. 23 years to phase out lead in petrol, but Thailand managed the feat in five years and now China aims to get it done in less than four, Chinese officials say.

MELBOURNE- An Australian cosmetics company says it is under pressure to remove "Australian made" labels from its exports to Asia because Australia could be seen by consumers as a racist nation. The Body Collection Pty Ltd, which sells skin care products to retailers in five Asian countries, says some Asian clients wanted the labels removed in case shoppers shunned them.
MOSCOW - Russian tea consumption could fall seven to 12 percent as a result of import duty increases on packaged tea due to come into force on June 1, Russian tea industry officials say.
